measurement: secrets-exposure matches an EXHAUSTIVE enumeration of 15 literal patterns and, on the shipped path, never calls the model. Measured against a pinned dtale commit whose Flask session-signing key literal produces zero prefilter hits, plus an audit of every shape the CLAIMS row advertised.
spendNote: No key path, no model call, no recording. Patterns were extracted programmatically out of dist/analysis-engine/detectors/secrets-exposure.detector.js rather than transcribed, and replayed under this detector's own scan semantics (line-by-line, break on first match), which differ from IDOR's whole-content scan.

threeDefectsFound.1_falseClaim: The CLAIMS row advertised `OpenAI sk-*`. NO PATTERN IMPLEMENTS IT. Both the modern `sk-proj-...` and legacy `sk-...` forms match nothing. The only `sk`-prefixed patterns are stripe_live_secret (`sk_live_`, underscore) and anthropic_key (`sk-ant-api03-`). OpenAI is reachable ONLY through the separate NEXT_PUBLIC_* claim, via next_public_suspicious, when the variable carries that prefix. This is a deletion, not a narrowing.
threeDefectsFound.2_categoryVsEnumeration: The CLAIMS category head reads 'Hardcoded API key / token / signing-secret literals', which promises a class. The implementation is 15 fixed literal patterns with no semantic credential recognition and, on the shipped path, no model stage that could supply one.
threeDefectsFound.3_baselineProvenance: The 20/20 baseline was measured with the LLM path ON and does not describe the shipped emit path. See baselineProvenance below.

theBound.statement: SecretsExposureDetector.analyzeFile matches only PREFILTER_PATTERNS. When llmValidation is false -- the shipped default, since FIXOR_SECRETS_LLM_OPT_IN is unset -- it takes the bypass branch (preFilterReason 'llm-bypass'), emits a finding built from the matched pattern's hand-authored explanation at confidence 'high' and severity 'critical', and never constructs a callClaude request.
theBound.consequence: A credential shape absent from the enumeration is invisible, and a shape present in it is reported at critical with no adjudication of whether the match is a real credential.
theBound.epistemicStatus: The MECHANISM is certain and read from source. The FREQUENCY of unmatched credential shapes in real codebases is n=1 case and is NOT asserted.

pinnedCase.whyThisCommit: The last commit carrying the literal. Fixed in 32bd6fb4a63de779ff1e51823a456865ea3cbd13 (CVE-2024-3408, GHSA-v9q6-fm48-rx74). Full SHA used deliberately: an 8-character abbreviation is not an identifier.
pinnedCase.whatItIs: A fixed Flask session-signing key shipped in source. Anyone can forge session cookies. The advisory is titled 'Authentication bypass in dtale'; the code is a hardcoded signing secret.

shippedButUnclaimed: google_api_key (AIza*) and stripe_live_publishable (pk_live_*) are implemented but NOT advertised in the CLAIMS row. They were deliberately NOT added to the row in this change: adding an advertised capability is governed by rule 1 of 'When this file changes', which requires a positive fixture, a negative control and a fresh baseline. Recorded here so the asymmetry is visible and can be closed on purpose rather than discovered again.

controlReEarnedOnThisInstrument.why: A control earns belief only for the instrument and the semantics it ran under. The 2026-08-16 control ran on these same secrets patterns but belief was then transferred to the IDOR instrument, which was broken. It is re-run here rather than inherited.
controlReEarnedOnThisInstrument.conclusion: The instrument produces non-zero on adjacent lines in the same language, so the dtale zero is a property of the pattern set and not of the harness.

baselineProvenance.finding: That run used the LLM path. The log header records SYSTEM_PROMPT fingerprint 24b91c16fa48 and every one of the 10 positives is adjudicated 'LLM:vuln/high' with model-written reasoning. The shipped path never constructs that call.
baselineProvenance.isTheFlipVerdictPreserving: YES on this corpus, and the same log proves it: all 50 negative runs (10 fixtures x 5) were deflected BEFORE the model -- 25 'pre-filter:no regex match', 20 'pre-filter:server-only marker', 5 'pre-filter:path filter'. Zero negatives reached the model, so no negative verdict depended on model judgment.
baselineProvenance.whatTheNumberCannotSupport: The corpus contains NO negative fixture that produces a prefilter hit and should nevertheless not be flagged. On the shipped path every prefilter hit becomes a confidence:'high' severity:'critical' finding with no adjudication. So 20/20 is silent on the false-positive behaviour of the path customers actually run. Reasoning TEXT also differs between the two paths and is not covered.
baselineProvenance.dispositionOfTheNumber: Preserved, not replaced, and annotated in place -- following the 2026-08-09 auth-bypass ANNOTATION precedent in the same file.

surfaceAudit.rule: Rule 3 of 'When this file changes' requires auditing every customer-facing surface when advertised capability moves.

surfaceAudit.inversionWorthNoting: docs/mintlify/detectors.mdx already stated 'secrets-exposure is regex-only by default and emits deterministically without an LLM call', while the scope contract that the same page says 'wins on any conflict' was silent on it. A reader following that instruction to the authoritative file found LESS truth than the summary. Edit A closes that inversion.

whatThisDoesNotEstablish: Nothing about how often unmatched credential shapes appear in real codebases. n=1 case.
Nothing about the bypass path's false-positive rate, which is unmeasured and is named as deferred work in the pull request body.
Nothing about the other five detectors.
Nothing about detection quality. The detector was never executed; this measures pattern reach, not judgment.
